sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Link previews: a Wikidata item's window (Space) shows its statements, its picture, every identifier as a link in three groups that fold (Music, Libraries and authority files, Other) with a filter, and its Wikipedia articles; a Language choice switches the names. A Wikipedia article's window shows its infobox, its opening, the other languages, and its sections, each read into the window when you open it. Links inside both open in the same window. The cards stay as quick as before. The identifiers' filter marks what it matched. In a window's path, every step on another site (Wikidata, Wikipedia, setlist.fm, Brucebase, any page; Discogs keeps its own marks) starts with that site's icon, and so does a MusicBrainz URL's ("[info]") step, with the icon of the site it names (the icons the cards and windows already show; a hover asks for none). Resting on such an icon shows a card: which site it is, what the step shows and how it was read (through Wikidata's, Wikipedia's or setlist.fm's API, from the page itself …), and that the icon is the site's own, asked once and kept for a month. A click on the icon opens the site's home page in a new tab (the pointer shows a finger there, as on MusicBrainz's own icons).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Link previews: setlist.fm links (a setlist, an artist's setlists, a venue) get a card and a window from setlist.fm's own API, with a free key of your own (new setting: setlist.fm API key, kept like the Discogs token: never exported). A setlist shows its songs by set, the encore too, covers with their original artist linked to MusicBrainz, guests, songs from tape and the show's notes; an artist's or a venue's window lists their setlists 20 at a time with "Load 20 more" and counts the tours, venues or artists of what is loaded. Links inside open in the same window. Without a key nothing changes.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Link previews: in the window of a MusicBrainz artist, place, label, event or any other entity, a link to another site (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Discogs, YouTube, setlist.fm, any page) opens in the same window, with Back, instead of a new tab. Ctrl-click still opens a new tab.
